Cc: legal@crestbank.com

Subject: Temporary retention exception: KEK lineage and rotation logs

Hi Jonas,

We have a live investigation that requires us to retain wrapped key lineage and associated rotation logs for an additional 90 days beyond our usual tenant retention window. We raised this with our internal controls team, and they requested the following from Redwood to complete the legal hold: 

- Formal confirmation that private key material will not be exported in plaintext (we expect only wrapped keys / key identifiers).
- Rotation log excerpt showing the KEK wrap events (UTC timestamps, HSM op id, operator id) for the last 6 months.
- Attestation that the KEK wrap used HSM-protected key material and the wrapping algorithm (AES-GCM / RSA-OAEP, whichever applies).
- An ACL/operator list for any personnel with wrap/unwrap privileges.
- A signed temporary retention exception form (we attached our form — crestbank_key_retention_exception_form.pdf) or a mutually-signed DocuSign link.

We also need a point of contact at Redwood who can walk our controls team through the artifacts and answer questions for our SOC2 audit window. Can you confirm what you can provide and an ETA? Ideally we need the artifacts by EOW (Fri 2028-06-02).

Thanks,
Emily Park
Sr. Security Program Manager
CrestBank

Hi all,

Attaching the rotation excerpt and a UI screenshot that shows the retention flag that will be toggled for CrestBank’s tenant. A few notes to answer the checklist from Emily: 

1) No plaintext export: we never export unwrapped private keys. The artifact we provide is the wrapped KEK lineage (wrap tokens + key identifiers) and a signed audit trail. We can include the HSM attestation statement for the wrap key.

2) Rotation log excerpt: attached kek_rotation_log_excerpt.csv contains (UTC timestamp, op_type, hsm_op_id, key_id, operator_role). Sample rows below (sanitized):

2028-03-12T22:03:41Z,wrap,op-9f4c34,KEY-7a1b,rotation_operator
2028-04-10T02:18:09Z,wrap,op-abb2f1,KEY-7a1b,rotation_operator
2028-05-02T14:49:56Z,wrap,op-c1d334,KEY-7a1b,rotation_operator

If you need full operator identities we can provide them under NDA or limited-scope disclosure to your audit team.

3) Wrapping algorithm / HSM: KEK wraps are performed inside our FIPS-validated HSM cluster (model: YubiHSM-2 / vendor attestation available). Current wrapping uses AES-GCM-256 for symmetric KEK wraps; cross-region transport uses RSA-OAEP wrapping for the transport envelope. I’ve included the short attestation paragraph we typically share in SOC2 packets.

4) ACLs & separation of duties: operator_role entries map to a permissions matrix where only rotation_operator and key_admin have wrap/unwrap rights; shift logs and operator separation checks are enforced by HSM operator tokens and 2-person ceremony for certain high-value ops.

Attachments: kek_rotation_log_excerpt.csv, screenshot_key_policy_ui.png

Let me know if CrestBank wants the logs delivered to a secure SFTP or a pre-authorized, time-limited Share link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Engineer (Crypto & Inference)
Redwood Inference
